name: Bernadette 'Bunny' Shearer
equipment: Leather jacket, brown, an Army Air Forces flight jacket with the patches taken off
Snub-nose .38, 5 rounds loaded, in the jacket's map pocket
Tire iron, under the driver's seat
Lulu: a 1941 Ford coupe, black, rebuilt by hand with a flathead V-8 that is not the one it came with, a police-band radio she is not supposed to have, and a hidden compartment under the rear seat
Studio transport pass: CASTELLANE PICTURES - TRANSPORT - SHEARER, B. - ALL GATES
A sealed envelope from Vivian Lark: 'Bunny, if I'm not back by the premiere, give this to Abel Kurland.' Inside, unopened: the claim check for Union Station locker 212
Road map of Los Angeles County, annotated in pencil with every shortcut, alley and police call box she knows
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin: +2 Dexterity, +1 Charisma. In Los Angeles she knows every alley and whose bar is whose; advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city, and once per foot chase the GM gives her pursuer the next complication)

Behind the Wheel (advantage on Driving checks in chases and to avoid crashing. Car: Lulu, a 1941 Ford coupe; in Lulu add 10 to the car's hit points and her proficiency bonus to its AC while she drives, and once per long rest when Lulu would drop to 0 hit points she drops to 1 and keeps running; she repairs Lulu on a short rest with no check)
Smooth Ride (her passengers don't have disadvantage firing from the moving car, and have advantage on saves in a crash or ram she is part of)
Lead Foot (bonus action on her turn: Dash, Disengage or Hide on foot, or one extra driving maneuver: a sharp turn, a sudden stop, or putting the car between her passengers and the shooting)

Nobody Looks at the Cabbie (Cab Driver background: she knows every street, shortcut and hotel doorman in the city, doormen and cabbies tell her who went where, and behind the wheel of a cab she can wait outside a building for hours unnoticed)

personality.traits: I don't talk about passengers. I drive with one wrist and I know exactly what's behind me at all times. I name every car I've ever loved.
personality.ideals: You get in my car, you're mine till I let you out. Nobody touches you on my watch.
personality.bonds: Vivian Lark. I've driven her to the lot every morning for two years. On Sunday the fourteenth I drove her to Union Station and she made me promise not to tell. I've kept it nine days and it's killing me.
personality.flaws: I'll take any dare that involves a car, and some that involve other people's cars.

appearance: Twenty-six, wiry, a cap of short dark curls under a newsboy cap, grease under her nails, a chipped front tooth from a stunt in a serial. She wears trousers and a man's flight jacket and nobody at the studio has told her not to for two years, because she's the best driver they have.
backstory: Bernadette Shearer was born in Lincoln Heights, the fifth of seven, and could drive her father's ice truck at twelve. She drove a Yellow cab through the war when the men were gone, then talked her way into the Castellane transport department in 1945 and into stunt driving a year later: she rolled a car for a serial and walked away, and the second-unit director has asked for her ever since. She has driven Vivian Lark to the lot every morning since 1945, and they talk the whole way. On Sunday 14 September Vivian asked to be driven to Union Station at night, gave her a sealed envelope and made her swear. Bunny has the envelope in her jacket. The transport dispatcher's log shows Car 11, Shearer, out to Union Station; when the party reads it, Bunny will have to decide.
